EventNotes:
Welcome to Cross Camp - four nights of cyclocross racing at the iconic Driveway in Austin, TX.

The rules are simple:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. Abide by all USAC cyclocross rules.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced.
  5. Please inform the finish line judges if you withdraw from the race.
  6. Prizes will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories.
  7. Please patronize our sponsors.
  8. You must check in with the registration staff to be counted in the results.
  9. Absolutely no alochol is permitted on the grounds of The Driveway at any time. 


Entry Fees

Entry fees are $45 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4 /Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

Season passes are available and will automatically enroll you for 4 nights of the category of your choosing. You may also select additional races throughout the series during your registration if you would like to race multiple categories on some (or all) nights.

Late registration is available this year. Entries after 12 pm the day of each race will incur a $5 late fee and may not be included in call ups. Registration closes 15 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can!

Racing Licenses

All categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org. 

Course

You will race on +/- 1.5 mile courses taking in new trails connected by fast pavement for a course that's always changing.

 

Parking and directions

Ample parking is available at the Driveway, but we highly encourage you to ride to the races. Please drive slowly on Delwau Ln, respect the venue, their neighbors and be cognizant of bicycles and pedestrians.

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

Producers

This event is produced by Camp of Lamps LLC and Holland Racing LLC.

ZAC Outdoors is beyond honored to host the annual Gravel Big Brutus race series here at Big Brutus. Big Brutus, located in West Mineral, Kansas, is one of the most iconic landmarks in the Midwest and home to the “Worlds Largest” electric mining shovel that bears its name. As one of the largest shovels of its kind ever built, it stands as a monument to the region’s rich coal mining heritage. Set against a backdrop of rugged terrain and scenic rural roads, the area offers a premier gravel adventure characterized by rolling hills and a course that honors the hardworking history and larger-than-life legacy of Southeast Kansas. Plus, what better starting and finishing line than the worlds largest electric shovel??

Deer Lake Outdoor Center is our host for the third year on 250 bucolic acres of deep woodsy new england nostalgia.  There are bunk houses and lean-to's that are available first come first serve, and so so many stellar private camp spots peppered throughout the property.  Click around on that link to check out the expansive space.

see you at the end of october!

Mass start at 8:00 am

Dirty Dozen  is a unique  cycling challenge. What makes this unique, you ask?  This is a multi hillclimb event of some of the steepest hills in the country with neutral disposition between hill segments, a rolling start into the hill, and a roadrace style finish for points.( if you are competing).  Whether you are a newbie or a seasoned competitor, this ride can put you to the test. Some basic ride details and rules follow. Additional information can be found at the main event web page: http://www.dannychew.com/ddinfo.html

Route:  Strava Route   This link is good for training purposes in small groups.  It may be updated at the last minute to account for road construction.  It has all the hills, but it may not be the course followed by every ride leader.  Competition heats in particular will follow different routes to Canton and Boustead.   

Number Pickup: This year you can pick up your number and possibly some swag at Biketek in Squirrel Hill an Forbes Ave from 5 pm to 7pm on  Friday October 23rd.  It will be warm and dry. By doing this you can avoid the cold line at the park in the morning.

Number Pickup link ( old)

If you elect to wait until Saturday morning the number pickup and Registration will open for 1 hour starting at 8am.  Bikereg will be live until the start.  No cash.

Start Location: This year’s start is located at the Rhododendron Pavilion in Highland Park.  This is on Lake Dr near the lake.

Parking:  There is plenty of parking on either side of the street along Lake and Reservoir Dr.  Please be respectful of the Dog Park and leave space in front for other patrons.  

Safety: Remember—safety first. You will be on open roads with vehicle traffic. Always be alert for road hazards and traffic. When riding in a pack remember that you are among cyclists of all different abilities. Follow instructions given by ride leaders and marshals in your group.

Weather: This is Pittsburgh.  Although the October event should prevent a whole day of snow or freezing rain,  it is still known to be wet and chilly at this time of year.  Dress in layers with a waterproof layer on top if necessary. Remember to overlap the waterproof layers so that water does not flow into your clothes...think roof shingles.  

You are responsible for determining when the weather has gotten the best of you.  Have an escape plan if things get unsafe for you or others. I do not think there are 400 Ubers in Pittsburgh.

Your numbers: For non-competitors, a helmet sticker will be provided. Competitors also receive frame,  bar numbers, or saddle numbers (TBD). The helmet number is to be mounted on the front, center of your helmet, just above the brim. The frame number is to be mounted towards the front of your bike’s top tube where it is clearly visible from either side. These will be needed for identification throughout the ride, and are essential for participation in the points competition.

Heats:  This year there may be as many as 9 heats including  a separate heat for the women's competition and a handcycle heat. Come to the Start line 5 minutes before your start time.

Heat 1: Open Competition (9:00am)

Handcycles. (9:00am)

Heat 2: Licensed ( 9:10)

Heat 3: Club Heat (9:15)

Heat 4: Women's  & Nonbinary Competitive (separate) (9:20)

Heat 5: DD Fan Club (9:25) 

Heat 6: Rouleur (9:30) 

Heat 7/8: Party Bus (9:40)

Food stops and restrooms: Food stops and portable restrooms are at Millvale Riverfront Park, on River Front Drive in Millvale, and at after Boustead at the Pauline St Park. The Cobden Street Block Watch and the South Side Slopes Neighborhood Association will provide some refreshments at the top of Eleanor Street, the 12th hill.

Being an official finisher: You must successfully ride every hill in the event to be an official finisher. Successfully riding a hill means that you make continuous uphill progress to the top under your own power, and the only contact points with the ground are the two wheels; falling down, putting a foot down, grabbing poles or other stationary objects, jockeying in place, etc. are disqualifying, and the hill must be restarted from the bottom if any of these occur. “Finisher” ribbons will be awarded to riders certifying they successfully rode every hill. To receive one, ypu will need to follow the provided route to the Awards Ceremony location ( East End Brewery)

Points competition: To remain eligible for a placing in the points competition, riders must be official finishers as described above and finish the final hill within 20 minutes of the first finisher of that hill. The pace between the hills is neutral and riders must stay together. When approaching the start of a hill, riders must stay even with or behind the riding official who signals hill starts.  This is a rolling start.  We do not stop at thebottom, or time your results. The official blows a whistle at the beginning of each contested hill at their discretion as they approach the bottom of the hill. Only then may riders go as hard as they want to the top in an attempt to score points. The first ten competitors in each competative heat on each hill receive points in their respective competitions.

After Party and Awards Ceremony will (Likely) be held at East End Brewing Company on Julius St in Larimer.  

The GPS route ,linked above Will directing  you back to Highland Park will lead you past the awards ceremony location.

The Final letter sent the day before the event will have all the latest information such as route, rest stops, schedule, locations, in case they change.

The Relentless Run & Ruck Challenge-October 24th, 2026

The Relentless Run and Challenge is a timed competitive-style endurance event built for runners and ruck athletes. 

You can choose to run it normally (no weight) or ruck style with weight. 

Either way you're on the same trail course, pushing yourself and getting after it!! 

Course Format and Event Options: 

The Course: One, approximately 5K loop on trails.
 

Event Options: 

5K: One loop. Great for first timers, fast runners, or anyone who wants to send it.

10k: Two loops. The sweet spot- competitive, challenging, and super doable.

Relentless 6-Hour Endurance Challenge: Complete as many 5K loops as possible in 6 hours. This is the long game option: pacing, grit, and staying disciplined when it gets hard. Perfect for anyone who wants to test themself at a longer time domain/distance.

Divisions (All Distances) 

Choose a division when you register: 

Run: Run it like a normal 5K, 10K, or 6 Hour Race. No weight, just run. 

Ruck: 30lb (Men)/ 20lb (Women) 

All Ruck weights are dry weight and do not include water. See additional details below.

Scoring and Results: 

  • 5K/10K: Ranked by fastest finish time 

  • 6-Hour Endurance Challenge: Ranked by total distance completed. Tie breaker: final fastest complete loop 

    Awards/categories will be finalized based on participation 

Ruck Standards & Rules (Weighted Divisions)

Mandatory ruck weigh-in will take place before the start and at the finish line.

Weight Rules & Approved Ruck Set Up

  • Required ruck weight must be non-consumable and non-wearable. No food, water, or clothing used as required weight
  • You can carry extra supplies (food, water, layers, etc.) Just know this counts as additional weight on top of the required division weight
  • Required weight must be carried on your back as a traditional ruck. Any backpack/ruck is acceptable. Plate carriers are NOT allowed
  • No sling bags or duffel bags
  • No trekking poles allowed
  • If you have questions about your ruck set up, email katie@stay-relentless.com 

Who This Is For

The Relentless Run & Ruck Challenge is for runners who want a simple, timed event, ruck athletes who want a legit course and standards, and anyone who wants to push themselves and have some fun..

Whether you’re chasing a time, carrying weight, or just here to test yourself - this challenge is for you.

All fitness levels are welcome - come push yourself and see what you’re capable of.

Non-Profit Donations: For each participant of the Relentless Run & Ruck Challenge $20.00 will be donated to to Heroes in Transition thanks to our community impact sponsor "Alquist 3d".

 

This a Festival, it is going to be fun.

Ride the Midwest's Most Scenic Fall Adventure!

Cross the Mississippi by ferry. Climb bluffs painted in peak autumn color. Ride rustic roads through two states in a single day before celebrating with delicious local food, craft beer, and fellow cyclists in the town where Iowa started!

Registration Includes

  • Ferry Fare
  • Aid stations fully stocked with Fall favorites
  • Five timed segments competitions (KOM, Sprint, Descents, Overall) for competitive riders
  • Finish line meal and post-ride celebration
  • Professional SAG support
  • Donation to local brain health initiatives
  • Professional event photography

Award Categories

The Fall Fondo features 12 timed segments spread throughout the route: 4 climbs, 4 sprints, and 4 descents. Awards will be given in 5 categories:

  • General Classification: Fastest male and female rider over all 12 segments
  • KOM/QOM: Fastest male and female ride over the 4 climbs
  • Sprint: Fastest male and female rider over the 4 sprints
  • Cannonball: Fastest male and female rider over the 4 descents
  • Young Rider: Fastest male and female rider aged 23 and under over all 12 segments

Aid Stations and Finish Line Party

Three aid stations will be fully stocked with beverages and food to keep you going, and don't forget to take in the views while you refuel!

Once you're finished, hang around at our finish line party and enjoy tasty local fare and brews!

Ride Routes

About BrainBike USA

BrainBike USA is a Dubuque-based organization that exists to promote cycling as a tool for improving brain health. We partner with local nonprofit organizations that invest directly in brain health initiatives, as well as with local cycling organization to expand access to bikes and bike-related education for our community.

5 Points 50 is Chattanooga's oldest mountain bike race that traverses Lula lake Land Trust and Cloudland Canyon State Park trail systems across Lookout Mountain. Whether you're in it to win it or want to ride the party pace with your friends, this race has a little something for everyone! With a 50-mile and 25-mile option, Racers will enjoy a grueling course packed with single track, climbs, downhills, rock gardens, and smooth flowy trails. Starting at Lula Lake Land Trust’s Core Preserve, riders will quickly begin making their way to the 5 Points Trail system and Durham Mine Trails, then back to LLLT via the Cloudland Connector Trail and Moonshine Trails. This race is sure to bring incredible views, amazing trails, and a heck of a good time!
 

Spectators are welcome on Saturday at no cost. Food and drinks will be available for purchase. If spectators want to camp they can purchase just a camping ticket.

 

 

Note: Camping is family-friendly.

Newest Categories:
Party Pace - This category is for those who want to enjoy the iconic trails and party but without racing. Party Pace riders will NOT receive a race bib or be timed. This is strictly for those wanting to enjoy the course at a leisurely pace. If you want to ride at a leisurely pace but still have your time accounted for, you should sign up for your age category! Party Pace riders still have to finish by the 4:30 cut off time. 

E-Bike Open - Class 1 Electric pedal assist only. No throttle bikes are permitted. There will be a riders agreement that everybody stays in Class 1 mode. This means no exceeding 20 miles an hour assist.



 

A Kids' Fun Ride (not a race) will be taking place (add-on registration required).

 

Lula Lake Land Trust has officially taken over the 5 Points 50 race as a fundraiser for the organization. Roost Racing approached LLLT in 2023 about transfering the race and LLLT accepted as an attempt to keep this iconic race alive, as well as raise critical funds for our trail building and maintenance efforts! 
 

All proceeds from the 5 Points 50/25 support Lula Lake Land Trust’s trail building and maintenance. Lula Lake has built over 60-miles of trail on our properties across Lookout Mountain, including the Moonshine trails, Cloudland Connector Trail, and the Durham Mine Trails. Your participation in this race (and all of Lula Lake’s races) goes directly back into our trail maintenance and construction efforts! 
 

What’s Included? 
Every Racer gets a custom 5 Points 50 t-shirt if registered before 10/10/26 and post-race beer/soda and food. 
 

Add-ons are available for camping, which includes a Friday night group ride.

Race Details:
50 Mile Course (3,500+ ft. elevation gain)
The 50-mile course starts with a 5-mile ride down Hwy 157 (Lula Lake Rd.) to the Durham Mine Trails. At Durham, racers will enjoy both single and double track trails before crossing over into 5 Points and then riding to the Ascalon trailhead. From there, riders will head back towards HWY 157 and cross over the highway to continue on the 7-mile High Point section (CCT) until you hit the Nickajack Parking Lot. Racers will then go down Nickajack road for .25miles to the F4 Trail. From here, you will ride through LLLT’s Core Preserve trails and Moonshine Trails to the finish. 

GPX file for the course 50 MILE COURSE. PLEASE BE AWARE that the mileage is not exactly accurate and the elevation could be more. This is JUST FOR REFERENCE. All racers are to follow course tape instead of the GPX file. Course markings rule the roost! The Land Trust section of the course is private and NOT to be ridden unless it is an open gate day. 

https://ridewithgps.com/embeds?id=52272426&sampleGraph=true&type=route

 

25 Mile Course (2,300+ ft. elevation gain)
The 25-mile course will begin with about 5 miles of riding down Hwy 157 (Lula Lake Rd.) to the Connector Trail road crossing, at which point you’ll turn left onto the connector trail. Riders will weave their way through LLLT’s (mostly single track) Core Preserve and Moonshine trail systems to the finish. The 25 mile course is the same as last year where it takes a left off the road onto Longbranch Connector. The 25 mile course is the second half of the 50 mile course. For the GPX file, please refer to the GPX link for the 50-mile race - the back half will be the 25-mile course. Again, follow course tape!
Ride with GPS 25 mi course

 

Aid Stations: 

50 mile:

Aid 1: Ascalon parking lot. Mile-21

Aid 2: Again at Ascalon parking lot. Mile-26

Aid 3: Longbranch Community Driveway. Mile-37

Aid 4: Lula Lake Land Trust core property. Mile-43


25 mile: 

Aid 1: Longbranch Community Driveway. Mile-11

Aid 2: Lula Lake Land Trust core property. Mile-16.5

Please be respectful of race officials if you are asked to drop - no discussion. You will be provided with transportation back to the start/finish.

Drop bags and pickup: 
The enforced drop-bag deadline is at 8 AM ET at check-in.

The 50-Mile course includes 4 aid stations, the 25-Mile course includes 2 aid stations. Our Aid Stations are well stocked with
hand off water bottles, fresh water, Tailwind and snacks. Be sure to carry with you the hydration and nutrition you require according to your training and health needs. Bags must be dropped by 8 AM ET on Saturday morning. Each racer is allowed two (2) one gallon drop bags that we'll provide at packet pick-up. Drop bags can be picked up after the race at the check-in table. 

There are NO refunds or transfers.
We do not have the capacity to mail awards, shirts, forgotten gear, etc. Pickup at LLLT offices can be arranged.
Deferrals are only offered in certain medical situations, please reach out to inquire.

We will do a podium for all categories, but not all category winners will receive prizes!

If you are absolutely unable to make check-in, you MUST: 

1. Contact us info@lulalake.org to notify us. We'll send you a waiver. 

2. Give the waiver to a friend to deliver to us during check in. Make sure you send your drop bags, as there is no way to deliver them to the Aid Stations on race day. Your friend MUST pick up your race packet with your race number in it and get it to you before the race starts! If you do not have someone deliver the waiver and/or fail to get your number from your friend, you will not be able to race.

Join us for the fourth annual Baileys Dirt Fondo and Fundraiser on Saturday, October 24th, 2026! 

 

Our “Dirt Fondo” is adapted from a traditional Italian “Gran Fondo,” and will feature a singletrack adventure race consisting of casual riding between optionally-timed “segments” and Strava KOM/QOM segment challenges. Rest stops throughout the courses will feature local treats to keep you energized for the trail ahead. Don’t miss out on your chance to support and explore the Baileys Trail System this fall!

 

The Baileys Trail System is an 88-mile mountain-bike-optimized trail system in the Wayne National Forest. Baileys Trail System will be the longest contiguous mountain bike-optimized trail system east of the Mississippi River. Visit our website to learn more about the trail system: www.baileystrailsystem.org/

 

All proceeds from the Dirt Fondo will support the management and development of the Baileys Trail System, the work of the Outdoor Recreation Council of Appalachia (ORCA), its nonprofit partner Athens-Wayne Outdoor Asset Development Corporation (AWOADC), and our mission: "To integrate conservation, outdoor recreation, and economic development to strengthen and inspire communities in Appalachian Ohio. Learn more about ORCA and our work: www.orcaohio.com/

Race Timing:

Race segments will be automatically timed. The overall course time will be timed for the Youth/Family ride. The overall course time will be timed for Black, Blue, and Green courses, but will not be judged for the sake of scoring. 

 

Segment timing is optional and can be selected during registration. All riders will be issued a timing device and number plate. For those who elect not to be timed, your name will be removed from the final results. Use of the timing device is mandatory and will be used to manage rider safety regardless of if the rider chooses to show their name in final results.

 

Participation in the KOM/QOM segment challenge is optional. To participate, riders should record and upload their ride to Strava upon finishing. Riders must upload their ride within 30 minutes of finishing in order to be eligible for KOM/QOM prizes.

 

Participants will be issued a number plate, which should be placed on the headset/handlebars of their bike with the provided zip ties. Participants will also be issued a timing device that must be worn on the left ankle (opposite the derailleur). After the race, the participant may dispose of the timing device. The number plate can be used as a meal ticket at the finish line. Race organizers will collect number plates for reuse after they are used as meal tickets.

 

Race Scoring:

For the youth course, the team with the fastest average time will win. The top three teams will be honored on the podium. Selecting team members and a team name is required during sign-up.

 

For the Green, Blue, and Black courses, segment placement rankings will be combined into an overall score, and the individual with the lowest overall score will be the winner. Podium awards will be issued to the top 3 competitors in each category. 

 

KOM/QOM segment challenges will not be factored into overall podium placements. A prize will be issued to the top KOM and top QOM on each segment, regardless of race category. KOM/QOM participation is optional, and participants must upload their race to Strava within 30 minutes of finishing to be eligible for prizes; they must also have their Strava privacy settings updated so that segment times are publicly viewable.

VELO AMIS PRESENTS THE FIFTH ANNUAL HALLOWEEN VICTORY TOUR 10/24/2026
ALL RIDERS GET A VELO AMIS GIFT and A FREE BEER or NON-ALCOHOLIC DRINK
(Rider Gift guaranteed for first 180 riders) 
 NEW FOR THIS YEAR, WE NOW HAVE 3 ROUTES! SEE BELOW 

NOT ROAD BIKE FRIENDLY - DON'T BELIEVE THE RIDE WITH GPS “SURFACES” 

REGISTRATION AND EVENT START:
Registration 9 am - 9:50 am
All riders must depart by 10 am

WHERE:
This scenic ride begins and ends at Victory Brewing Company in Parkesburg, Pennsylvania and will highlight a portion of the Enola Low Grade Bike Path. 

WHAT:
This ride begins and ends at Victory Brewing Company, and travels through Lancaster and West Chester counties. The routes are almost entirely on rural roads and bike paths. The Enola Low Grade Bike Path is approximately 8 miles from Victory Brewing. THE 50 and 35 MILE ROUTES HAVE MORE GRAVEL, HILLS AND SCENIC ROADS IN ADDITION TO THE ENOLA BIKE PATH.

DISTANCES:
Distances are the Halloween Victory Tour Long (50M), Medium (35M) and Short (27M). 
NOTE that the 27M is an out and back.

Routes are subject to change. Routes are not considered final until they are sent out to pre-registered cyclists following the close of pre-registration. DO NOT BELIEVE THE RIDE WITH GPS ROAD vs GRAVEL - it is NOT accurate. Believe us when we say - PLEASE DO NOT choose a road bike for this event. A gravel bike or mountain bike with a less aggressive tread would be the best choice. 

ROUTE AMENITIES:
The 27 Mile and 35 Mile routes will have 1 aid station each at approximately Mile 12 and Mile 22 respectively.
The 53M route will have 2 aid stations at approximately Mile 16 and Mile 36.
Aid stations will be well-stocked with goodies to keep you moving through the route.
The route will be well-marked, however, you are ultimately responsible, so please download maps and cue sheets and GPS files (will be sent to registered riders once online registration closes). We will NOT have Cue Sheets for you at the event, please print your own or download the PDF file of the cue sheet and save paper. The event director may alter the proposed routes due to acts of nature, road closures, and/or local recommendations. 

Remember, this is not a RACE. Enjoy a ride taking in the history and culture of Lancaster and West Chester counties with your friends, family, and perhaps new friends you meet along the way. We are riding on routes / bike paths that have many other users.  

REGISTRATION INFORMATION:
Ride is limited to 300 riders
Sorry, no refunds. Please see Route Change & Transfer Information below to see your options.  We are a 501c3 organization and your entry fee becomes a donation. Please purchase insurance through BikeReg if you are looking for a refund option.

PRICING:
$65 ($55 UNTIL 6/15/26)
Day of: $75
19 and Under: $20
Military or First Responders: Contact us for $20 registration

ROUTE CHANGE AND TRANSFER INFORMATION:
Sorry, no refunds will be available.
Transfers between cyclists are allowed via BikeReg and can be done by the registered cyclist for a $5 fee until pre-registration closes. Category changes are allowed at no charge and can be done by the registered cyclist until pre-registration closes on BikeReg, and at the event.

HALLOWEEN FUN:
It is Halloween and we encourage all riders to wear a costume for the Best Costume contest! Two winners, all riders are welcome to participate, so have fun!

THE GOODIES:
All riders will receive a rider gift (mugs guaranteed for first 200 riders), a ticket for 1 free beer / non alcoholic drink and post ride snacks. Stocked aid stations and a well marked course as well as great riding scenery!  

GPS Files/Cue Sheets:
Final Cue Sheets and GPS files/Maps/RideWithGPS will be emailed to riders within 24 following the close of online registration. Please be advised that route changes may be made depending on local requirements or local road conditions. The event director may alter the proposed routes due to acts of nature, road closures, and/or local recommendations. The route will be well-marked, however, you are ultimately responsible, so please download maps and cue sheets and GPS files. We will NOT have Cue Sheets for you at the event, please print your own or download the PDF file of the cue sheet and save paper. Make sure that you add mail@BikeReg.com to your email safe sender list.  All rider communication is through BikeReg.

WHY:
This year, know that whatever route you ride, you'll be supporting Velo Amis and our Mission. This year we will ride to remember our friend, Dave Troop. We will continue to support the Enola Low Grade Trail and The Hellbenders mountain bike team. Please read more about Velo Amis and our Mission and who we Support.  

Maps:  
FINAL ROUTES WILL BE EMAILED TO YOU AFTER THE CLOSE OF REGISTRATION
 

Other Rules & Guidelines:
- Unfortunately we are not able to allow “children’s bike trailers” for the ride. We feel that this ride is not appropriate for children in trailers. On the other hand, if you are riding with your child on a pull behind bike where the child is pedaling (similar to a tandem bicycle) this is allowed. We appreciate your understanding. Note that your child will need to be registered (small fee to cover insurance). Contact us to register a child on a trailer bike.
- Do not bring outside alcohol to the brewery.
- Follow the rules of the road. Routes will be open to traffic. Please, NO headphones. Please ride single file and be courteous to other users. All routes are on heavily used bicycle and walking paths. We want to be invited back, so please be good stewards!
- Bike helmet required.

EventName: Arkansas Enduro Series | Round 3 | Gudrun Enduro @ Gudrun MTB Festival
EventNotes:
HOT SPRINGS ENDURO | OCTOBER 24-25, 2026

The Hot Springs Enduro takes place in the Northwoods Trails system located in Hot Springs National Park. This trail system houses well over 30 miles of trails ranging from beginner green trails to double black for the experts out there looking to push the limits. The AES Enduro is being held in conjunction with the Gudrun Mountain Bike Festival - a three-day mountain bike festival featuring dual slalom, Strider races and the Atilla the Hun XC races. There’s something for everyone. Come for AES and stay for the rest.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

  • One-day competition with up to 4-7 stages and 10-20 total miles of rider-designed racing with dedicated pre-race practice times the day prior to the race.
  • Sufficiently marked courses with maps emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Lively mid-race aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 5 deep.

RACE VENUE

Cedar Glades Park - Enter on Trapper Lane from Wildcat Road

Race Venue Address - 461 Wildcat Rd, Hot Springs, AR 71913

 

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When permittable, an official pre-ride/practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances.

FRIDAY 

  • Early pre-riding is allowed although some stages may in the process of being finishing marking.

SATURDAY 

  • 9AM-4PM | Check-In & Official Practice Day

SUNDAY

  • 8AM - 10:30AM | Timing Chip Pick-Up according to Wave Times. Late Check-In available.

    • RIDER MEETING: 8.45AM

    • PRO & EXPERT CATEGORIES: 8:00AM-8:45AM CHIP PICKUP | 9:00AM START

    • INTERMEDIATE CATEGORIES: 9:00AM-9:45AM CHIP PICKUP | 9:45AM START

    • BEGINNER CATEGORIES: 9:45AM-10:30AM CHIP PICKUP | 1O:30AM START

  • 9AM - 3:30PM | AES Gudrun Race Day

  • 4PM | Enduro Awards at Venue Podium

Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When possible, an official practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances. 
 

LODGING - When it comes to lodging in Hot Springs, you have a plethora of options to choose from. From trusted hotels to cozy vacation rentals, you’ll find a perfect place to stay in Hot Springs. For a comprehensive lodging guide visit hotsprings.org.

DRY CAMPING - When possible, limited dry camping spots at the Race Venue will be available to reserve during event registration. Please refer to the event’s online registration service for additional details.

RESTAURANTS - In Hot Springs you can refuel with BBQ, pizza and a local micro brew, fresh catfish or homemade taffy. Visit hotsprings.org for a few ideas. We'd break the internet if we listed them all. 

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In October, Hot Springs, Arkansas, experiences mild and comfortable autumn weather. Daily highs average around 77°F (25°C), cooling down to average nighttime lows of about 53°F (12°C).

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

NICE TO HAVES - Bug spray, sunscreen, spare tubes, pump or CO2, plugs, patches and other parts.

DOGS - Dogs are allowed but are required to be on a leash at all times. No exceptions.

TRASH - If you pack it in, pack it out. We are guests. Please follow all event sustainability and recycling requests.

RACE DAY MEAL - A post-race meal will be provided to racers and volunteers on Race Days only. Redeemable meal tickets will be provided at the Registration & Timing tent. When possible, additional food trucks and other resources will be made available on-site for fans, family and friends.

WAIVER - All participants will be required to sign a waiver of liability prior to competing in the Arkansas Enduro Series.

REFUND POLICY - Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine, and refunds will not be issued except under extreme circumstances. The Event Organizer reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances including rescheduling the event to a future date.

If participants choose to add additional Registration Protector through BikeReg, those claims are handled entirely by Allianz Global Assistance. For policy questions or to file a claim visit www.eventregistrationprotection.com or call 1-888-799-2832.

SERIES RULES - additional series information and rules available at www.arkansasenduroseries.com/rules.

Updates: please join our Facebook page, where all updates will be made https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=61578481500522                                                                                 Please join us on Instagram @pocono.cyclocross.classic

Registration: Online registration closes at 10:00PM on 10/22/26. Multiple races will cost an additional $10 for each race (the discount will be applied when you check out on Bikereg). Racers under 18 years old must have a parent sign the waiver. Day of registration is available for an additional $10 charge (cash only).  Registration opens at 8:00AM and closes 30 minutes prior to each race. No Refunds Will Be Issued.  Numbers will be on the Left Side. 

Licensing: USA Cycling Permit #16085.  All racers must have a valid USA Cycling permit and have it with them at registration.  A one-day beginner USA Cycling license is available for $15 (cash only) at registration. 

Staging: Racers should report to the staging area, next to the skatepark, 15 minutes prior to their race.

Call ups: All pre-registered racers will receive a call up.  Call ups will be be based on the following order 1) PACX standings (first 8 in standings) 2) Crossresults standings 3) Order of registration.  Day of registration will be staged in the back of their respective category.

Lapped Riders: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leader.  

Course: This course will be centered around a levee on the Broadhead Creek in Dansbury Park.  Riders will be on mixed surfaces, mainly grass, during the race and will be challenged by elevation changes as the course navigates on and around the levee.  There will be one run-up and one set of barriers.  The course will start with a short prologue and then run in a clockwise direction.  A full lap is approximately 2.5 KM or 1.6 miles in length.  A course preview video is available on our Facebook page and Instagram page.

Pit: A double-sided pit will be available.  Once your race is over, please remove your items.  

Team Tents: An area will be available near the pits for team tents.  There will be no cost but please message us via the ‘contact us’ button at the bottom of this page, so we can reserve your spot.  We will have 10 Team Tent spots available, which are located next to the pit. 

Parking: Please follow directions from staff.  You may be directed to park outside of the main parking area, if the main parking area reaches capacity.  Looking at the map below, we will use parking #1 first.  If we fill this up, we will then utilize parking #2.  Parking #2 provides parking, head on, in front of the Day Street Center and the basketball courts.  If needed, we will then utilize parking #3.

Rules: No alcohol permitted. No offensive language or unsportsmanlike conduct will be permitted. Helmets are required whenever you are riding a bicycle.

Restrooms: Porta-potties will be available near the start and near registration.

Timing, Results, and Podium: Timing and results will be orchestrated by Main Event Timing.  Results will be published on their website: https://my.raceresult.com/timers/4408/   A 15 minute protest period will follow the release of results.  Once the results are finalized, no changes may be made.  A podium presentation will be made following the 15 minute protest period.

Pavilion: A large pavilion, at Registration, will be available for your use.  Feel free to set-up your trainers under the pavilion. 

Title Sponsor: UESCA - United Endurance Sports Coaching Academy LLC     https://uesca.com/

When you register, you will be entered to win a free coaching certification from UESCA.  This is a $599 prize that will be awarded to one lucky racer!!!   UESCA is a global leader in endurance sports education.  We will announce the winner after the race!!!!

Sponsors:

Pocono Bike Club        Pocono Bike Company        Lamprey Systems         UESCA

Stroud Region Open Space and Recreation Commission         East Stroudsburg Borough  

Yogaversity             BevCity Brands

Thank you: We would like to extend a thank you to Mike Festa for all of his behind the scenes help.  While Town Hall Cross is on hiatus, Lamprey System's course stakes and barriers live to race another cyclocross race at PCCX; thanks Greg! A huge shout out to PACX for allowing us to be part of this long-time series.  The Pocono Bike Club is our local club; thank you for all of your support to bring this event to the Poconos. The use of Dansbury Park would not be possible without the support of East Stroudsburg Borough and the Stroud Region Open Space and Recreation Commission.  Lastly, thank you to the racers who come out and support grassroots racing!

Hi all! We're very excited to see you again!  

The Great Pumpkin Ride is sponsored by the Fauquier Trails Coalition, a non-profit organization, and is a fundraiser for the construction of new trails throughout scenic Fauquier County.   

The Great Pumpkin Ride will be held October 24, 2026 this year and is a rain or shine event.  

IMPORTANT DATES: 

  • October 02, 2026 - Last day to register and guarantee shirt size

  • October 10, 2026 - Registration Closes

  • October 21, 2026 Last day for online transfers.
    • Emergency transfers must be requested via email after this date.
  • October 23, 2026 - Early pickup event shirt/wristband location/time - Blue Ridge Cyclery in Warrenton from 3:00pm to 6:00pm
    • You may still pickup your paperwork/shirt the morning of the event but we HIGHLY encourage you to come to early pickup. We promise you will be glad you did!
  • October 24, 2026 - Great Pumpkin Ride 2026!

IMPORTANT: In an effort to ensure everyone receives the GPR shirt they select upon registration, there will be absolutely NO exchanging of shirts at registration or at early pickup. The shirts are long sleeve performance style. Same as years past. Do your best to get the size you think you need.

Registration is online ONLY and the field is limited to 1,300 riders. Registration fee is $85.

Registration includes:

  1. ONE long-sleeved technical UNISEX shirt. There will be NO size-switching at registration!  
  2. Up to three rest stops (depending on the ride distance you select) with the Great Pumpkin foods you've come to know and love.
  3. SAG vehicles for rider support and minor mechanical issues provided.

TRANSFER RULES:

NO TRANSFERS after October 21, 2026

The Fauquier Trails Coalition does not broker transfers (we simply don’t have the volunteer staff to handle the brokering of transfers).  If you want to transfer your registration, your best bet is to post on our Facebook page.

Here is the general transfer procedure:

Replacement (new) rider –

1.  Find a rider who is looking to transfer their registration (see above).

2.  Make arrangements to pay the original rider for their entry fee.  (The original entry fee transfer must be handled separately and privately between the two parties, and outside of BikeReg.  

3.  Contact the original rider to transfer the registration to you (see instructions below)

4.  Follow the email link you receive and complete your information. Once you've completed the process, the original rider will be removed and you will be added to the list of registered participants in their place.

Original (old) rider –

1.  Find a rider who is looking for a transfer registration (see above).

2.  Make arrangements to transfer/receive payment from the new rider for your entry fee.  (The original entry fee transfer must be handled separately and privately between the two parties, and outside of BikeReg.)

3.  Go to this link: https://www.bikereg.com/great-pumpkin-ride and enter the email address of the person you're transferring your entry to.

4.  Once the new rider accepts the transfer, you will be removed from the event and the new rider will be added to the list of registered participants in your place. 

And finally . . . the roads for the Great Pumpkin Ride are NOT CLOSED!!  Please exercise caution and common sense.  If it doesn’t feel safe to ride two abreast, it probably isn’t.  And riding more than two abreast is not permitted in Virginia (and ticketing cyclists isn’t an unheard of occurrence – just be aware).

See you at the start!

The 12 Hours of Old El Paso or 12 HOEP is a team relay or solo racer mountain bike event held on the northeast of the beautiful Franklin Mountains, in El Paso, Texas. It is brought to you by EP Outdoor Adventures. The venue is at the Bowen Ranch Roundhouse.   This year our race will be held rain or shine on Saturday, October 24, 2026.  While this is a race, it's also an amazing day on the mountain to make new friends and spend quality time with your fellow mountain bikers as well as with any outdoor enthusiasts!

The Bowen Ranch Roundhouse has been purchased by Texas State Parks, so participants will need to get their daily access permit. If you will be camping you will also need to obtain the camping permit and display it on your dashboard. We will be verifying all permits as required by the State Park and we will do this during packet pickup to make it easier. NO PERMIT, means NO RACING! Thank you for your understanding.

COSTUMES

Besides our awesome race course, one of our greatest attractions are the costumes that our competitors come up with for the event.  They can get extremely creative with their individual or team costumes.  Prizes for the best overall costumes!

RACE START
12 hour race starts at 9:00am

The race will utilize a Lemans style start. The Lemans start ensures a safe and exciting method for starting a large number of riders. It consists of having all the riders line up at the starting line, at which time a pistol is fired. The racers will then run to their bikes, mount up, and enter the race course. All starting riders must have their bikes pre-positioned and be logged-in prior to the start of the race.  Racers that begin the race wearing a costume will get a headstart.  All riders on deck (those riders who are waiting for their teammate to complete a lap) must wait in the Pit Zone area and be ready for the transition.

RACE FINISH

The end time for the race is 9:00pm. All laps that count towards the final position standings must be completed by 8:59:59pm.  This means that if a racer finishes his lap at or after 9:00:00, the lap will not count.  The final finishing places are to be determined by the total number of laps completed and the order in which each team completed the final lap.  This means that if there is a tie in the number of laps completed, the tie breaker will be decided by who finished the laps in the fastest amount of time.

THE COURSE

The course is about 12.5 miles in length, and consists of smooth, fast flowy trail, short sections of small-to-medium rocks, fast descents, short steep climbs, mellow rolling single track, berms, gravel roads, a few arroyo crossings, and more. All-in-all it is one of the fastest, smoothest, least technical race courses in our area!

THE RULES

All participants are required to have a trail-worthy mountain bike, helmet, and bike light to compete.

Riders must be registered. No poaching please. It's rude.

Be courteous. There are plenty of passing opportunities on this course but if you must pass right this minute, please do so in a kind way. If you have a mechanical, please repair it on the side of the course and allow riders to pass easily.  All racers must conduct themselves in a civilized manner. Use of foul or intimidating language or behavior towards anyone including other racers or volunteers on or off the course will not be tolerated. Any racer found in violation of this rule will be penalized. This penalty may include the immediate disqualification of the racer and/or their team.  We're all out here having a good time!

Be a good person. No littering, help out if someone is in need, use restrooms where available, smile and say thanks to all of the great volunteers out on and off the course.

No riding in the Pit Zone.  Succinctly put, No riding in the Pit Zone.

Riders pushing bikes or slower riders must yield the right of way to racers riding bikes.

Lap Rules. When you reach the pit area, you MUST dismount your bike and approach the check-in staff before you or your partner can go out for the next lap. No check-in = No lap registered! If you decide that you are not going to continue, please let a race official know in the main pit area.

Riders who are checking out, must do so at the Check-In table in the Pit Zone.  High-five, handshake, slap, or kiss your partner to make the exchange legit. If you leave before making contact with your teammate, your team could be sanctioned with time. In general, we always want to know when you are coming or going.

Lights Required. All racers will finish in the dark, so lights are required. All participants riding at 5:00pm and after will need to use a working handlebar or helmet light. Anyone found riding with their lights off can be disqualified. Please remember to turn lights off when entering the exchange tent. 

No Headphones or Bluetooth speakers . Due to the nature of our course we need to have all of our riders alert and able to hear when other riders are approaching.

Federal, State, and local ordinances must be always followed.

All bicycles must be completely human-powered. Pedal-assist bikes or E-Bikes are not permitted on State Parks.

Pets.  All dogs must always be on leashes for the safety of the riders and everyone else.

REFUNDS/CREDITS
No refunds will be issued in case that the event must be cancelled due to uncontrollable circumstances including, but not limited to restrictions set forth by the State of Texas. The promoter reserves the right to make accommodations as it may deem fair or equitable in the event of an unexpected event cancellation.

DAY-OF REGISTRATION IS NOT AVAILABLE
On-site registration is not available, so please do not ask.  You MUST pre-register online.

PARKING
Car pooling is highly recommended as parking is limited at the Roundhouse area.

AID STATIONS

This is not a marathon race so there will NOT be any aid stations out on the course. You will be responsible for carrying enough water to sustain yourself. For solo racers (and anyone else who needs it), there will be opportunity to place water and food at the event grounds for you to grab as you pass through.

CAMPING

It's a long day on the bike, and the race doesn't end until 9:00pm, so kick back, relax, and spend some quality time with your teammates and the fat tire community. 

Primitive tent camping is permitted on State Park grounds if you are not obstructing traffic or racers.

The State Park grounds are not shaded, so if you want shade, you'll need to bring canopies and/or pop-up tents to provide shade. All tents and canopies must be secured to the ground.

We will have additional Port-o-johns for restrooms.

FOOD

A food truck will be out there in case you need to purchase some grub. 

Bring your own food and drinks.

VOLUNTEERS
Interested in volunteering? We need volunteers to help make this a successful event.  Please contact Mario Lopez lopezmario100@yahoo.com

EventName: Brutiful Cape: Gravel Bike & Fat Bike Adventure Rides - Oct 24 & 100 Miles for Fat Bikes Oct 25
EventNotes:
These are incredible gravel and fat bike rides in an area where riders get to experience all sorts of cool trails, back roads, and dirt roads that weave their way all over the Cape! Riders who select gravel rides won't be riding on beaches. Those who select fat bike options will have the opportunity to experience awesome beach riding in addition to the cool mixed terrain that this area serves up and few people know about.

For all Saturday riders who aren't camping Friday evening: We have secured parking within 0.4 mile from the campground so it won't take long to get from your car to the start!

We're offering a camping option at checkout so you can stay overnight right at the ride start & end at a nice campground if you prefer.

The Cape at this time of year is serene, it's not yet closed, but it also doesn't have many people on the beaches or trails. Roads are quieter than they are during the summer as well. 

Get your friends together to spend a fun weekend camping, enjoying the peace of the Cape, and memorable riding!

Riders will enjoy hot coffee and tea in the morning before rolling out and seasonally appropriate food (a hearty meal) at the end of the ride  (read: hot food if it's a chilly day!) Around a hot fire in a comfortable setting.

Complete details are on the Ride Page.

Hi friends, unfortunately I’m going to have to put this years event on hold after a crazy year in the food truck biz.  I’ve had no time to focus on getting this event together and it wouldn’t be right pressing send on something I know wouldn’t live up to the last years.

I don’t like to do things half-assed, and with only 3 weeks left until the event date, it would have definitely been sub par in my books and it’s not the way I want to remember it.  I’m flying out to Europe on Halloween and I need to focus on getting a roof on my house before I leave because it’ll be winter when I return.

This will be a transition year and I’m thinking of just sending everyone out a course gpx file and we all go out for a ride at our own pace.  I’ve never had the chance to ever ride the course in one shot with anyone and perhaps this could be the year!

Next year I’d like to return to the 2-day format and what it was originally intended to be - a gravel cross event.

Stay tuned on updates but I refunded all of you who were registered.  My apologies and my thanks to your commitment!  Enjoy a few memories from last year.

Cheers,

Chris Gagnon

EventName: Northeast Velodrome Try the Track Clinic - 10/24/2026
EventNotes:
This is a track riding and racing clinic for riders who are not familiar with riding a fixed gear or riding on a velodrome. Track racing has some peculiarities that make it a little different from road riding or racing.  This clinic will give you the knowledge and experience necessary to begin track riding at the Northeast Velodrome.

The course consists of 3 sets of skills:

  • Riding a fixed gear
    • Getting started and stopping on a fixed gear bike
    • Spinning and controlling your speed with your pedals instead of brakes
    • Practice riding close to another rider
    • Learning to hold a line while continuing to pedal through
  • Track riding conventions and etiquette
    • Learning how it feels to use the banking and the turns
    • The terminology of the track lanes
    • How to move and communicate with the other riders on the track
  • Paceline and racing skills
    • Learning how to use the turns and the banking of the track to form and hold a pace line
    • Taking a turn on the front and then moving out and up and back to take a place at the back
    • Learning race rules for various track events

At the end you will have the knowledge and some experience of track riding. You will understand how riding a fixed gear on a track differs from road or mountain riding with a freewheel and brakes.

The course fee includes rental of a track bike if needed. If you are renting you need to bring pedals and shoes. A helmet is required. Please indicate your frame size, and if you know it your saddle height, measured from the center of the crank axle to the top of the saddle.  This is not required but will aid in preparing the bike and speeding the sizing process.

Price: $30 - Field limit of 8.  Rental is included.  Successful completion of this course certifies you to ride any other events at the Northeast Velodrome.

THIS EVENT IS RAIN OR SHINE!

Day Of Registration:

While we strongly encourage you to preregister (and greatly appreciate you doing so as it helps the event go more smoothly), there will be "day of" registration. It will be an extra $10 after 6pm Saturday evening, and will close 60 minutes before the start of your event.

Race day Schedule:

  • 9am plate pickup opens
  • 9:30am Cat 3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race day of registration closes
  • 10am Cat3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race start
  • 11:30 am plate pickup closes.
  • 11:40 am Jr Novice podiums and riders Meeting
  • 12pm Cat 1 categories start
  • 12:40pm All remaining cat 2 and cat 3 categories start. THIS TIME IS APPROXIMATE!
  • 2:30-3pm, all podiums.
  • Adaptive racers, we may alter where in the schedule you start as we work with you and learn what works best. 

!!!!!!!Start time notes!!!!!

In an effort to offer a safer and more fun race environment for all participants we are now starting Cat 2 and Cat 3 racers after Cat 1 and E Bikes have completed one lap. This greatly reduces conflict between very fast cat 1 and E Bike racers passing novice racers by nearly eliminating lap traffic. The posted start time of 12:40m for cat 2 & 3 is approximate. We will begin releasing the remaining cat 2 & 3 waves after Cat 1 racers go through scoring. Know your wave number!

10am Cat3 Jr. Novice Races

You may have noticed that we are doing Cat3 Jr novice races early in the day and be asking "hey, what's up with that?" We want to give Jr's, and particularly novice Jr's the best race day experience we can. Separating the Jr. novice races to an earlier start allows us to do 3 things:

  • Fewer racers on course for the race.
  • For families where the one or both parents also race it gives the parents a chance to spectate and cheer their kids.
  • Novice Jr's get their own start, with more people cheering and spectating. Bring the cowbells!

USA Cycling Licenses, and NOMBS Series Championship rules & eligibility:

NOMBS is proud to be bringing a USAC sanctioned series to Ohio and be hosting the official USA Cycling Ohio MTB Championship. Partnering with USA Cycling helps us offer you a great series with structure, consistent categories & scoring, good insurance for landowners, and allows an opportunity for riders with goals outside Ohio to earn USAC points. 

USA Cycling Race Age:

 Your “race age” is the age you will be on December 31st. This rule exists so that a person does not have to change the age group they are entering partway through a race season. 

NOMBS Series Championship Eligibility rules:

  1. A rider must have a current USA Cycling License (need not reside in Ohio).
  2. Must race in the season finale race.
  3. Scored on best 5 races.
  4. In the event of a points tie the season final race is the tie breaker.

EventNotes:
In honor of Jarrod Bunk’s belief that the bike community can help to build a community in need, we bring back Higher Ground with the locals of Johnstown, the Pennsylvania Environmental Council, and the Community Foundation for the Alleghenies.

This will be a scenic tour with opportunities to connect with the natural beauty of the Laurel Highlands and bond with like-minded souls before and after in downtown Johnstown.

The goal is to keep the grassroots spirit of the original iterations of Higher Ground which showcased rugged routes throughout the surrounding Johnstown area. Expect to be greeted with punchy climbs, path-less-travelled trails, and a tour of the environmental wonders that are the Laurel Highlands and the Allegheny Mountains. 

Here are the routes that will be available:

  • Thirty: An out-and-back on the Path of the Flood and Staple Bend Tunnel trails to go to the Johnstown Flood Memorial Park (you'll ride through the dam that broke).
  • Forty: Heads north towards Hinkston Run Reservoir, then east on quiet paved roads before bombing down into Summerhill and into the Johnstown Flood Memorial Park (you'll ride through the dam that broke), and returning to Johnstown on the Path of the Flood and Staple Bend Tunnel trails.
  • Sixty: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown, then up into the Rager District climb & descent, and back into Johnstown.
  • Eighty: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown, and then UP into the forested Gamelands west of town and then back down to the rolling roads in the south before riding back to on the Jim Mayer Riverswalk and into Johnstown. NOTE: You must wear orange on your body and an orange helmet (or helmet cover) to ride this route.
  • Hundo: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown and then UP into the forested Gamelands west of town and then back down to the rolling roads in the south before riding back to on the Jim Mayer Riverswalk to the Start/Finish and the last 20 miles go up into the Rager District climb & descent and back into Johnstown. NOTE: You must wear orange on your body and an orange helmet (or helmet cover) to ride this route.

There will be aid station support and the start/finish venue will have food & drink available. All riders must check in & out so we know who's taking on which sections of the course.

To learn more about the history and purpose of Higher Ground, read this story on The Radavist from 2022.

Partners that are making Higher Ground happen include:

  • Pennsylvania Environmental Council
  • Community Foundation for the Alleghenies
  • Fat Jimmy's Outfiters
  • Thomas Automotive
  • New Trail Brewing
  • Endo TuneUp
  • Stan's
  • Nittany Mountain Works
  • Footdown.cc
  • Freeze Thaw Cycles
  • Hushmoney Bikes

Proceeds from Higher Ground will support The Women's Help Center and the Pennsylvania Interscholastic Cycling League.

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Additional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $30 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for late/day-of registration by Saturday 10/24 at 8:30 AM.  Check-in at the venue will open around 7:30 AM on event day.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race. There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Code of conduct: Racers and spectators are expected to abide by USA Cycling's code of conduct. Any behavior, sign, kit, etc., that discriminates on the basis of race, color, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, gender identification, or national origin, or that interferes physically with any race, will be met with ejection from the venue and disqualification from all races.

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. The minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

The collective teams comprising the MABRA Super Series are committed to providing inclusive and equitable racing events.  The Super Series is proudly adding non-binary categories (1/2/3 and 4/5) to race during the women's races.  This addition is to honor all of our cyclists and provide a category that allows everyone to race with how they identify.  In the event that USAC chooses to amend current policy to align with UCI changes for our transgender racers, then WTF (women-trans-femme) will be added to our non-binary categories as WTFNB.

Start Staging: Cat 5 Men & Cat 4/5 races = Registration order (HURRY…the first race is on BikeReg!). All other fields: Super Series standings for first row (8 racers), Crossresults.com for the rest of the field. Be at start staging 15 minutes before your race start or risk losing your spot.

Series Points:  Weekly Super Series points are awarded for ranking to the following fields – Men Cat. 1/2/3; Women Cat. 1/2/3; Masters 40+ Cat 1/2/3; Masters 50+ Cat. 1/2/3/4; Masters 60+ Open; Master Women 45+/50+/60+, Cat. 1/2/3/4; Men Single speed Open; Women Single speed Open; U19 Junior Women and U19 Junior Men. Youth Categories will receive overall series point leader jerseys following the last race @ Cap Cross Classic.

See the BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series website for complete rules and regulations for series points.  Points calculated at Crossresults.com.

Directions: Once arriving at the fairgrounds entrance, follow the parking volunteers to the designated parking area. Parking of vehicles or trailers will not be permitted in the team pits. Traffic is one-way only! You will enter and go right down the road to the parking area. Once leaving the parking area you will exit on opposite side you entered and leave going left up the hill. Please follow the signs.

On-Course Warmup: Riders shall only enter the course for warmup laps between races in the designated area near the starting grid.  Race officials will designate time and length of pre-rides.

Pit: There will be one double-sided pit on course. Please remove your equipment immediately following each race to make room for others. UPDATE - ONLY valid USAC license holders may enter the pit and provide support for racers. No spectators or non-licensed persons will be allowed in the pits. Please see a USAC Official if you have questions.

Course Description: The course will utilize multiple areas of the fairgrounds, including grass, pavement, dirt, gravel, barns, the ever so fun happy humps and barriers. There may even be a surprise or two!

The course will consist of a mix of grass, a small section of paved walking path, and a good chunk of the wooded disc golf course. Feedback from 2025 was taken into account some small changes will be made including but not limited to: No turns on the disc golf tee boxes, additional tape in the woods, possible relocation of the finish if we can find a good spot.

 

Helmets must be worn at all times and absolutely zero alcohol consumption on borough property. 

Registration will open an hour before the first race, day of registration is available, cash only. Promotor has the right to combine categories based on registration numbers, etc.

Licensing Requirements:   This is a USA Cycling sanctioned event. All riders must present a valid license at registration and sign an event release form (minors must have a parent/guardian sign).  One-day and annual licenses will be available for purchase at registration. Junior discounts only applicable to junior race fields. Current USAC Fee Schedule here. https://usacycling.org/memberships-old/one-day-licenses

Call-up Protocol:  Call ups will be given based on NJBA Standings and rules. Above all we will use promoters discretion. If you yell at the promoter you will go to the back. 

Lapped Riders:  Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them. Laps are pretty fast on this course, and come in around 7-8 minutes. 

Results:  Results will be posted at the registration area.  Results will be made final 15 minutes after being posted.  The top 3 finishers in every event must report immediately to the start/finish line for awards and photos.

E-BIKE REGULATIONS (THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS....LEARNING AS WE GO....)
As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
 
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race

PLEASE CHECK INDIVIDUAL RACE EVENTS ON BIKE REG, WEBSITE AND FACEBOOK GROUP FOR RACE TIMES & MORE DETAILS AS EACH RACE APPROACHES.
www.monthofmud.com

Lastly, this is the MoM, let's have some fun!

Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 8:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 6:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: JUMP BASICS & JUMP PROGRESSION SUN OCT 25th
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

 

 

 

JUMP BASICS: 

We get it, everyone wants to jump! However, most people don't embrace the technique AND psychology behind doing it well. You have to understand the what and why before you can start to build confidence with the how, that's what this session is for. Not only will you build a solid understanding of what NEEDS to happen, you'll also get plenty of reps working through the steps of how it needs to happen, all in a safe and controlled environment. 

Topics Covered: 

Riders will get plenty of reps on multiple takeoffs/landings and Rich will work through multiple rounds of video so you can see exactly what's working and what isn't. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and Skills Park Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Our Pro level coaches break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 70 years experience, they guide you through their real world experience and give you key insight and cues on what to do and also what not to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

REGISTRATION NOTES: 

  • Online registration closes at 11:59PM on Friday prior to race day.

  • No refunds due to buyer's remorse/if you are unable to attend.

  • In the unfortunate event that we are forced to cancel the event due to COVID, inclement weather, or other circumstances beyond our control, the race director will seek to refund entry fees, but cannot refund BikeReg fees.

  • 2nd Race Only $10 if you register in the same transaction. You pay full price for the more expensive race.

  • No outside alcohol will be permitted! Alcohol and food will be available for purchase at Sycamore Speedway. 

LICENSES: All races will be held under USA Cycling (USAC) permit. Riders without an annual USAC license will be required to purchase a 1-day license for $15. Renew your annual license online at http://www.usacycling.org/.

All USAC rules apply. Helmets must be worn at all times.
